title: Fuzzy rollforward playpad
body:
Quick brain-dump / proto PRD for a small, user-facing experiment: Fuzzy Rollforward.

Goal:
- Reduce visible interruption and error surface when a long streaming generation is interrupted (OOM, node preempt, network blip).
- Make partial outputs useful and safely stitchable so client apps can present an interim answer and continue generation seamlessly.

Motivation / context:
- Customers complain that a single failure late in a long response is jarring (entire response disappears or restarts).
- Dedicated customers want predictable UX when we switch fallback model variants or fall back to cached prefixes.
- We already stream tokens; this is about making state transfer and resume tolerant to missing suffixes and mixing model variants.

Assumptions (needs validation):
- Most end-user UX is OK with an honest intermediary message + incremental completion.
- We can persist minimal KV cache + request intent metadata cheaply for a short window (30s-5m).
- Model mismatches (tokenization/temperature) will cause differences but we can detect/score 'stitch quality'.

User stories (prioritized):
1) As an end user, when a long assistant reply is interrupted, I see a partial answer with a clear "resuming" affordance and the final answer completes in-place without losing context.
   - Acceptance: The client receives a finalization event that identifies whether the resumed portion is incremental or a fresh replacement.
2) As a developer, I can opt-in to "fuzzy_rollforward: true" per route and see metrics on resumed vs replaced responses.
   - Acceptance: API accepts flag; logs resume events; console shows resume rate and avg extra-latency vs baseline.
3) As SRE, we can trigger an automated fallback to a smaller model and still produce a coherent stitched answer rather than failing the call.
   - Acceptance: Fallback path increases success rate under degraded infra by >= 6% in small load tests.

MVP scope (minimum we can ship quickly):
- Server: persist ephemeral resume blobs (prefix tokens, last N KV cache chunks, request metadata) in a fast store (redis-like TTL 2 min).
- Client API: new event types in streaming: STREAM_PARTIAL, STREAM_RESUME_START, STREAM_RESUME_PATCH, STREAM_RESUME_END with a small semantic header.
- Resume policy: attempt same-model resume first; if unavailable, attempt compatible-variant with a 1-step soft prompt to align tone.
- Console telemetry: track resume_attempted/resume_successful/patch_quality_score.

Open design questions / tradeoffs:
- How big should the resume blob be? (full KV cache vs last-k tokens vs semantic summary)
- When mixing model variants, should we re-run a short re-generation over last 30 tokens to smooth style? Cost vs quality tradeoff.
- Security: should resume blobs be encrypted differently? (they live for a short TTL but may contain PII).
- Client compatibility: forcing clients to handle new stream events is heavy; can we present resume as a normal stream with a little wrapper meta?

Patch quality heuristics (proto):
- token-overlap score between pre-failure suffix and resumed prefix (if there is overlap)
- semantic similarity (cosine between embeddings of last 64 tokens and resumed first 64 tokens)
- abruptness penalty for immediate repetition or contradictory facts (lightweight NER mismatch)
- map heuristic to categories: GOOD / ACCEPTABLE / BAD and attach to resume_end event.

Experiments to run (A/B):
- Exp A: no resume (control) vs Exp B: resume with same-model KV rehydration. Measure success rate, avg perceived latency, user cancel rate.
- Exp C: resume with variant model + 10-token smoothing regen. Measure patch_quality and cost delta.

Metrics to log / dashboard ideas:
- resume_attempt_rate, resume_success_rate, mean_patch_quality_score, extra_tokens_generated_for_stitching, client-visible-delay_ms, resumed_vs_replaced_fraction.
- SLA impact: track 1p (hosted) requests that would have failed but were resumed.

System sketch (very rough):
1) Request arrives, stream starts, periodically snapshot small resume blob (every 3s or on N tokens).
2) On failure event from runtime: set resume_flag in RPC response, keep blob alive for TTL, emit STREAM_PARTIAL then END with resume_id.
3) Client reconnects (or server-initiated route) and calls resume endpoint with resume_id.
4) Router picks candidate backend: same model preferred, else variant policy, else fail.
5) Backend attempts to warm KV cache from blob (best-effort) then generate resume tokens, produce STREAM_RESUME_* events including patch_quality.

Security & privacy notes:
- Default behavior should redact any attachment content from resume blob for customers with PI-sensitive routes. Make this configurable per-org.
- Ensure KMS encryption at rest for resume blobs; auditable TTL deletion.

Rollout plan (phases):
- internal dev-only feature flag (2 weeks) => small infra changes, smoke tests.
- internal dogfood (redwood-team) with console metrics visible (3 weeks) => iterate heuristics.
- opt-in beta customers (4 weeks) => measure uplift and gather UX feedback.
- GA with on-by-default but kanban toggle for regulated accounts (dependent on legal signoff).

Risks / Failure modes:
- Poor stitching quality could produce hallucinations or contradictions (user trust hit).
- Cost increase due to extra regen steps and KV transfers. Need to cap extra token budget per resume.
- Complexity across private/on-prem deployments where resume blob persistence semantics differ.

Backlog / nice-to-have features:
- semantic-summary resume (store a 1-2 sentence compressed summary instead of full blob) to support long konversations cheaply.
- server-side auto-de-duplication to avoid repeating the same token chunk at stitch boundary.
- visualization in console showing before/after diffs for resumed responses.

Immediate next steps (for me):
- sketch minimal proto for resume blob schema (what fields, size cap) — due Friday.
- spike: implement tiny redis-backed blob store in sandbox, simulate resume with small opt-in client. (2 day spike)
- sync with Talia on UX affordance wording and Evan on metrics schema. Book 30m.

Notes to self (random):
- consider reuse of existing session-snapshot TTL paths (maybe junction with session-presets).
- check legal about storing short-lived user-generated content for 2min across multi-tenant hosted.
- think about making resume_id OpaqueHash rather than sequential.

Edits log:
- 2024-10-12 initial sketch
- 2024-10-20 added metrics and experiments
- 2024-11-01 reconciled with Talia feedback (UX language)

End of scratchpad. Keep terse and iterate.
